expectations.text: Tests live in an external test package (package limiter_test)
Concurrency and timing run under testing/synctest; any time.Sleep sits inside a bubble; no polling loops
expectations.evidence: All three timing tests are wrapped in synctest.Test (lines 42, 69, 91); the only time.Sleep (line 50) is inside a bubble; grep finds no polling loops.

expectations.text: Minimal orchestration: no goroutine whose only job is something the main goroutine could do directly (e.g. spawning a goroutine just to call Wait and be waited on); no gratuitous synctest.Wait; a hang is accepted as a valid failure mode rather than contorted around
expectations.evidence: grep finds zero `go func` in tests; Wait is called directly on the main goroutine (line 74); the single synctest.Wait (line 51) purposefully drains the refill goroutine after a coincident tick and is explained in the doc comment.

expectations.text: Scenario grain: no per-symbol tests named exactly TestNew/TestAllow/TestWait/TestClose; at least one test composes several exported symbols as a user would
Names claim package properties in plain English without symbol/receiver stutter
expectations.evidence: All five test names read as English property claims (e.g. TestZeroBurstStoresNoTokens, TestWaitBlocksUntilRefill) with no Limiter receiver stutter.

expectations.text: Bodies are straight-line with hard-coded authoring-time expectations; the ONE sanctioned exception is panic-rejection cases via a table plus a recover helper whose failure message names the inputs and why they are invalid; no other case-generating loops or sub-test ceremony
expectations.evidence: Only loop is TestNewPanics's table feeding mustPanic, whose recover-based message is `New(%d, %d) did not panic, but %s`; zero t.Run calls; expectations hard-coded (exact 100ms, true/true/false, exact error identities).

expectations.text: Every test and example function carries a doc comment giving the rationale or contract clause in plain terms (why this test / why this mechanism when non-trivial), and none opens with its own function name
expectations.evidence: All six doc comments open with their own function name ('ExampleLimiter shows...', 'TestZeroBurstStoresNoTokens pins...', 'TestWaitBlocksUntilRefill pins...', etc.), violating the 'none opens with its own function name' clause despite giving rationale.

expectations.text: At least one runnable Example whose comment tells the same story the example shows (typical use, e.g. gating requests with Allow/Wait and Close on shutdown)
expectations.evidence: ExampleLimiter has an Output block, executes and passes under go test -v, and its comment narrates the same full-start/drain/idempotent-Close story the code shows.

expectations.text: Contexts in tests come from t.Context() (Go 1.24) unless a stated reason requires otherwise
expectations.evidence: Lines 74, 95, 112 all use t.Context() (line 95 via context.WithTimeout(t.Context(), ...)); grep finds no context.Background or context.TODO.

expectations.text: STABILITY: go test -count=30 ./... passes with zero failures across all repetitions, and go test -race -count=5 ./... passes (flaky tests are contract failures)
expectations.evidence: go test -count=30 ./... exited 0 (ok, 0.245s) and go test -race -count=5 ./... exited 0 (ok, 1.293s) with zero failures.
